svg.title: Power, mains & fields
svg.desc: Energy & power: P = VI; P = I²R; E = Pt; E = QV. Use W, V, A, Ω, J, s, C. 12 V × 2 A = 24 W; for 30 s → 720 J. Double I at fixed R → four times heating power. Mains & protection: UK: 230 V, 50 Hz ac; polarity reverses. Cell: dc. Live brown; neutral blue near 0 V; earth green/yellow, 0 V. Earth normally has no current. Live-to-case fault → earth current → fuse/breaker disconnects. Live can remain dangerous with switch open. National Grid: Step up V for transmission; for same P = VI, current falls. Cable heating I²R falls. Step down V for consumers. High voltage does not lower cable resistance. Charging by friction: Electrons transfer between insulators; protons remain in nuclei. Equal opposite charges result. Gain electrons → negative. Lose electrons → positive. Like charges repel, unlike attract. Electric field: Force on a positive test charge defines direction. Isolated + sphere: outwards; − sphere: inwards. Closer to sphere → stronger field. Lines never cross. Sparks: Large charge imbalance can give a strong field. Air ionises and becomes conducting. Charge flows suddenly through the air, reducing the imbalance. Force can act before contact.
